Restrict an SDRF to the files one search read, and report what could not be placed

sdrf_restrict.Rd

Restrict an SDRF to the files one search read, joining each searched file to the row of its acquisition, and report what the join could not place.

Answers which rows of this SDRF did my search read? A search reads X-calib.mzML while the SDRF names the acquired X.raw. Calls mzLib's SdrfSearchScope.Restrict, which joins them by stem, ignoring case, after removing the derivative suffixes MetaMorpheus writes (-calib, -averaged, in any order and number). Each kept row is carried cell for cell, with the searched file's name in a new comment[searched data file] column directly after comment[data file]; nothing is renumbered.

Usage

sdrf_restrict(path, searched_files, out = NULL, limit = NULL, offset = 0, timeout = 60)

Arguments

path

Path to a .sdrf.tsv file.

searched_files

The files the search read, as paths or bare names, a character vector. Name an element by the acquired file it came from when you know it - c("X-calib.mzML", "X.raw" = "sample_A.mzML") - and that overrides the suffix rule for it; leave the others unnamed. Sent on stdin, one line each.

out

Also write the whole restricted document here as SDRF, whatever limit and offset are. Must end in .tsv; name it .sdrf.tsv, because mzLib adds that to a name that does not end in it. written$path names the file written.

limit

Maximum rows to return. NULL, the default, returns all of them.

offset

Rows to skip.

timeout

Seconds to allow, or NULL to wait indefinitely.

Details

Restrict first, then read a design. sdrf_design and sdrf_isobaric_design match searched_files by exact name, and key on comment[searched data file] when a document has it, so a restricted document joins the search's own file names.

Value

An mzlibr_restricted_sdrf, which is also an mzlibr_sdrf, so sdrf_value, sdrf_all and sdrf_records work on it. path is the SDRF restricted, as given; columns the restricted header, which may repeat names; rows one character vector of raw cells per returned row, in the input's row order - a kept row shorter than the header is padded with empty cells, so unlike sdrf_read the rows are never ragged. row_count counts the rows kept, in the whole restricted document, whatever limit and offset; returned_count the rows returned, starting offset rows in; truncated whether rows were left behind; input_row_count the rows of the SDRF before the restriction.

searched_files lists the searched files as sent, in order, and acquired_name_count counts the files you named an acquired file for. What the restriction could not place: searched_without_row, the searched files (file names) the SDRF has no row for - reported, never invented; dropped_data_files, the acquired files the SDRF describes that this search did not read (a row naming no file is dropped too, and not listed); ambiguous, acquisitions two or more searched files claimed, as "stem: searched, searched" - the first in name order kept the rows, and the others have none and are not in searched_without_row; and shared_stem, searched files whose rows name two or more different acquired files (one run listed as X.raw and X.mzML), as "searched: acquired, acquired", every such row kept. written is a list (path, the file mzLib wrote, and row_count, the rows of the whole document), or NULL without out. caveats says how the join works and what it cannot tell you.

Paths, on any platform

The searched files may be full paths; the join uses the file name. A path written with the other platform's separator (D:\search\x.mzML on Linux) is reduced here too, but the design readers split only the running platform's separator, so give sdrf_design and sdrf_isobaric_design paths as this platform writes them (file.path() does).

Wraps

Wire verb sdrf restrict. Generated from the bridge's verb spec sdrf.restrict.yaml (bridge commit 45833ca804d6) by scripts/build-man.R; the spec owns these facts, and all three bindings render the same ones.

  • SdrfSearchScope.Restrict in mzLib/Readers/Sdrf/SdrfSearchScope.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • SdrfSearchScoping in mzLib/Readers/Sdrf/SdrfSearchScope.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • SdrfDocument.WriteResults in mzLib/Readers/Sdrf/SdrfDocument.cs at mzLib d10017ce

Parameters: units, ranges and defaults

path

path; required. One .sdrf.tsv file, deposited, improved or drafted. A file that does not exist is a usage error.

searched_files (wire --stdin)

string[]; required; range >= 1 line of 1 or 2 tab-separated fields. The files the search read, one per line, as paths or bare names: searched, or searched TAB acquired when the caller knows the acquired file a searched one came from (MetaMorpheus reads it from an mzML's own sourceFile). An acquired name overrides mzLib's suffix rule for that file and may be given for some lines and not others; with none, mzLib is given no map (its default, acquiredNameOf = null). Blank lines are skipped and a UTF-8 BOM is dropped; fields are trimmed. No line, a blank searched field, more than two fields, or one searched file given two different acquired names (compared ignoring case, as mzLib collapses searched files) is a usage error.

out

path; default absent; range .tsv only, any case (PYB-4). Also write the WHOLE restricted document here, whatever offset and limit are, through mzLib's SdrfDocument.WriteResults: atomically (a temp file moved into place), CRLF line endings, a final line break. Must end in .tsv, case-insensitive, checked before the SDRF is read (bridge thread 010, PYB-4, as sdrf pool --out). A missing folder is created (PYB-5). mzLib adds .sdrf.tsv to a name that does not already end in it, so searched.tsv is written as searched.tsv.sdrf.tsv; written.path says which.

offset

int; in rows; default 0; range >= 0. Skip this many restricted rows in the payload. The file --out writes is never windowed.

limit

int; in rows; default absent; range >= 0. Return at most this many restricted rows. Absent means every row.

Returned fields

Each field with its type, its unit, and what NA means when it is NA.

path

string; never NA. The SDRF path as given.

searched_files

string[]; never NA. The searched field of every stdin line, trimmed, in stdin order, as passed to mzLib (duplicates included; mzLib collapses those that differ only in case).

acquired_name_count

int; in files; never NA. Searched files given an acquired name; 0 when none was, and mzLib was then given no map.

input_row_count

int; in rows; never NA. Data rows in the SDRF before the restriction.

columns (wire column_names)

string[]; never NA. The restricted header: the input's, with comment[searched data file] directly after comment[data file] and any earlier comment[searched data file] removed. A LIST that may repeat names, as for sdrf read.

row_count

int; in rows; never NA. Rows kept (SdrfSearchScoping.Document), before the window.

returned_count

int; in rows; never NA. Rows in rows.

offset

int; in rows; never NA. The offset applied.

truncated

bool; never NA. True whenever rows were left out by offset or limit, including an offset past the end.

rows

string[][]; never NA. One list of raw cells per kept row, row-major, as sdrf read shapes a document, in input row order. Never ragged: mzLib pads a short row with empty cells.

searched_without_row

string[]; never NA. SdrfSearchScoping.SearchedWithoutRow: searched files (file names) the SDRF has no row for. Reported, never invented.

dropped_data_files

string[]; never NA. SdrfSearchScoping.DroppedDataFiles: acquired files the SDRF describes that this search did not read, in row order. A row naming no file is dropped and not listed.

ambiguous

string[]; never NA. SdrfSearchScoping.Ambiguous: acquisitions two or more searched files claimed, as stem: searched, searched. The first in ordinal name order kept the rows.

shared_stem

string[]; never NA. SdrfSearchScoping.SharedStem: searched files whose rows name two or more DIFFERENT acquired files, as searched: acquired, acquired. Every such row is kept. The channel rows of one multiplexed file name one file, so are not listed.

written

object; NA when out was not given. {path, row_count}: path is the file mzLib wrote (the out path, plus .sdrf.tsv when it did not end in it); row_count is the whole restricted document.

caveats

string[]; never NA. Six static caveats.

Errors

Each is an R condition carrying the class shown and mzlib_error; see mzlib_error.

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

path missing or the file does not exist

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

stdin has no searched file; a line with a blank searched field or more than two fields; one searched file given two different acquired names

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

--out without a value, or not ending in .tsv (checked before the SDRF is read)

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

offset or limit negative or not an integer

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

the SDRF has no comment[data file] column (mzLib's ArgumentException), or mzLib cannot read it (MzLibException), or the --out folder cannot be created or written

mzlib_service_unavailable (service_unavailable)

Never raised by this verb.

Caveats

  • The join is by STEM, case-insensitively, after mzLib removes MetaMorpheus's derivative suffixes (-calib, -averaged, in any order and number), so X-calib.mzML finds the row naming X.raw. A searched TAB acquired line overrides that rule for its file. A row whose stem joins nothing is tried once more by an earlier search's comment[searched data file].

  • Nothing else changes: no replicate or fraction is renumbered. comment[searched data file] goes directly after comment[data file]; an earlier search's is replaced, because it is this search's field.

  • A kept row shorter than the header is padded with empty cells, so the document is never ragged, unlike what sdrf read returns for the same file.

  • ambiguous: the other claimants of an acquisition get no row and are not in searched_without_row. shared_stem: the document can describe one run twice, and only the depositor can say which row is right.

  • The design verbs match searched files by exact name. Restrict first: sdrf design and sdrf isobaric-design key on comment[searched data file] when a document has it.

  • --out writes the whole document with CRLF line endings, whatever the input used, and mzLib adds .sdrf.tsv to a name that does not end in it. Name the file .sdrf.tsv.

Performance

Every call starts one bridge process, which costs a .NET start-up before any work.

Same verb in other bindings

  • Python (pyMzLib): pymzlib.sdrf.restrict

  • Rust (mzLibRust): mzlib::sdrf::restrict_with with RestrictOptions

  • R (mzLibR): sdrf_restrict

Since

Wire protocol 1; pyMzLib 0.6.0; mzLibRust not yet shipped; mzLibR not yet shipped.

Not yet verified

The spec records these as open. They are listed rather than hidden:

  • PUSH-TO-MAINLAND: SdrfDocument.WriteResults returns nothing and adds .sdrf.tsv to a name not ending in it, so the bridge reports the path by mzLib's own test (ResultFile.CanRead) instead of being told. Ask mzLib to return the path written, or to refuse rather than rename. sdrf pool --out has the same rename and still reports the path as given.

  • No --paths-stdin form: stdin already carries the searched files, and one search restricts one SDRF.

  • SdrfSampleCopy (#1451, same PR) is not projected: it only feeds SdrfBuilder.Build, which is G-sdrf-verbs.

References

  • doi:10.1038/s41467-021-26111-3: SDRF-Proteomics, the format restricted (Dai et al., Nat Commun 12, 5854, 2021)

sdrf_searched_data_files, sdrf_isobaric_design, sdrf_design

Examples


# Two calibrated runs, the raw file of one of them as well, a renamed file whose acquisition you
# know, and one the SDRF does not describe:
pool1 <- "HJOS2U_20140410_TMTpool1_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr0"
pool5 <- "HJOSLO2U_QEHF_20150329_TMT_pool5_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr0"
searched <- c(paste0("D:\\search\\", pool1, "1-calib.mzML"), paste0(pool1, "2-calib.mzML"),
  paste0(pool1, "2.raw"), "sample_A.mzML", "not_in_sdrf.mzML")
names(searched) <- c("", "", "", paste0(pool5, "1.raw"), "")
scoped <- sdrf_restrict("PXD008841.subset.sdrf.tsv", searched, limit = 2)
scoped
#> <mzlibr_restricted_sdrf> PXD008841.subset.sdrf.tsv: 30 of 40 rows kept for 5 searched file(s)
#>   32 columns (some names repeat - use sdrf_all())
#>   30 rows in the document, 2 returned
#>   ! truncated - rows were left behind
#>   ! The join is by STEM, case-insensitively, after mzLib removes MetaMorpheus's derivative suffixes (-calib, -averaged, in any order and number), so X-calib.mzML finds the row naming X.raw. A searched<TAB>acquired line overrides that rule for its file. A row whose stem joins nothing is tried once more by an earlier search's comment[searched data file].
#>   ! Kept rows are carried cell for cell: no replicate or fraction is renumbered. mzLib adds comment[searched data file] (the searched file's name, no folder) directly after comment[data file], and replaces one an earlier search wrote.
#>   ! A kept row shorter than the header is padded with empty cells, so this document is never ragged, unlike what sdrf read returns for the same file.
#>   ! ambiguous: two or more searched files claimed one acquisition; the first in name order kept it, and the others get no row and are not in searched_without_row. shared_stem: one searched file joined rows naming two or more DIFFERENT acquired files (X.raw and X.mzML); every such row is kept, so the document can describe one run twice, and only the depositor can say which is right. A row naming no file is dropped without being listed in dropped_data_files.
#>   ! The design verbs match searched files by EXACT name. Restrict first: sdrf design and sdrf isobaric-design key on comment[searched data file] when a document has it, so the restricted document joins the search's own file names.
#>   ! --out writes the WHOLE restricted document, whatever limit and offset are, through mzLib's SdrfDocument.WriteResults: atomically, with CRLF line endings whatever the input used. mzLib adds .sdrf.tsv to a name that does not already end in it, so written.path is the file actually written.
#>   searched without a row: not_in_sdrf.mzML
#>   acquired but not searched: HJOSLO2U_QEHF_20150329_TMT_pool5_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr02.raw
#>   ambiguous: HJOS2U_20140410_TMTpool1_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr02: HJOS2U_20140410_TMTpool1_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr02-calib.mzML, HJOS2U_20140410_TMTpool1_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr02.raw
c(input = scoped$input_row_count, kept = scoped$row_count, returned = scoped$returned_count)
#>    input     kept returned 
#>       40       30        2 
sdrf_searched_data_files(scoped)
#> [1] "HJOS2U_20140410_TMTpool1_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr01-calib.mzML"
#> [2] "HJOS2U_20140410_TMTpool1_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr01-calib.mzML"
scoped$searched_without_row
#> [1] "not_in_sdrf.mzML"
scoped$dropped_data_files
#> [1] "HJOSLO2U_QEHF_20150329_TMT_pool5_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr02.raw"
writeLines(strwrap(scoped$ambiguous, 80))
#> HJOS2U_20140410_TMTpool1_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr02:
#> HJOS2U_20140410_TMTpool1_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr02-calib.mzML,
#> HJOS2U_20140410_TMTpool1_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr02.raw
